summary: Cycle detection outside Loop is dead: _upstream_closure memoizes a closure truncated by the per-path `seen` set, so _ordered_nodes never sees the back-edge and a cyclic graph is admitted with one edge silently dropped.
failure_scenario: Graph nodes [back, triage], connections triage->back and back->triage, input ISSUE: visit(back) caches closure[triage]=[] (back is in `seen`), so triage is ordered first and the back->triage edge vanishes. Admission succeeds and the sealed manifest contains no binding for it, instead of the intended 'cycle outside Loop' AdmissionError. The author's written topology is reinterpreted without a fault (I11/I13: no guess, itemized error).
evidence: Ran _upstream_closure on a 2-node cycle -> {'b': [], 'a': ['b']}, _ordered_nodes returned ['b','a'] with no error. Ran world.validate on the cyclic graph with test/back (BRIEF->ISSUE) and test/triage: ADMITTED, resolved_connections omit the back edge. No test in tests/runtime/test_validator.py or elsewhere (grep 'cycle outside') exercises the guard, so the error branch has never run. Pre-existing.

summary: _heartbeat_loop only handles OwnershipLost; any other exception silently ends the heartbeat task while the node keeps running, so the lease lapses unobserved and the failure surfaces only after RunSucceeded.
failure_scenario: A transient journal error on one heartbeat (e.g. sqlite busy) kills the task. _check_run_control only reads `lost` (never the task state), so the walker keeps executing a long node with an unrenewed 30s lease; a successor can claim the run and the physical side effects of the node are not fenced. The error is raised only in _stop_heartbeat during _finish_run, after the run has already committed SUCCEEDED, so the caller sees an exception for a run that is durably succeeded.
evidence: Probe with heartbeat_interval 0.02s, journal.heartbeat raising RuntimeError on its 2nd call, node sleeping 0.3s: heartbeat calls stopped at 2 (about 15 intervals missed), run state ended 'succeeded', _start_direct then raised RuntimeError. Pre-existing.

summary: Resume of a run that failed on a non-bool loop continuation re-raises ContractViolation from _inspect_loop_history outside any failure handling, leaving the run RUNNING with no RunFailed/LoopFailed.
failure_scenario: First attempt: member checkpoints exist, _loop_decision raises, LoopFailed + RunFailed recorded (FAILED). resume(): _execute transitions FAILED->RUNNING (RunResumed), then _execute_loop's up-front _inspect_loop_history replays the complete iteration and calls _loop_decision (walker.py:1067) unguarded, so ContractViolation escapes _execute/_drive. The run stays RUNNING, lease released, and every later resume repeats it; the live path converts the same error to LoopFailed but the replay path does not.
evidence: Probe with tests/runtime/test_loops.py non_bool_impl: first run FAILED; walker.resume(...) raised ContractViolation 'continuation must be exactly bool, received int'; journal run_state afterwards = 'running'. Pre-existing.

summary: registry_compare returns no change for versions whose bodies differ: composite Graph bodies and PythonRef package/module/qualname/contract_hash are never compared (source_digest may be None and then stringifies to 'None').
failure_scenario: Two retained versions of a composite with identical boundary but different internal graphs, or two atomic versions with source_digest None but different qualname, yield ComponentComparison.changes == {}. An operator or agent reads 'no changes' as identical before promotion or rollback (negative inference taken as affirmative evidence); metadata.labels and lineage are also omitted.
evidence: Registered two ComponentDef(test/pipe) versions (full pipeline graph vs graph with announce node removed, same inputs/outputs; content hashes differ) and called ControlPlane.registry_compare as a READ actor: result ComponentComparison with changes {}. No test references registry_compare. Pre-existing.

summary: A failed shutdown is latched: _shutdown_task keeps the failed task and state stays 'stopping', so retries replay the cached exception and never call RunHost.shutdown again.
failure_scenario: RunHost.shutdown raises once (e.g. transient error while draining workers). Every later ControlPlane.shutdown() re-awaits the same finished failed task, raising the same exception; the host is never retried, lifecycle never reaches 'stopped', and mutations stay refused. _startup_once has the same shape if abort_startup() itself raises (state stays 'starting', failed task retained).
evidence: Probe: patched run_host.shutdown to fail on first call; attempt 1 and attempt 2 both raised the same RuntimeError, host shutdown called once, state 'stopping'. Startup variant read from code only. Pre-existing.

summary: inspect_source's 'rewrites commit ancestry' guard checks only the loose refs/replace directory and info/grafts, so replace refs held in packed-refs (and a shallow file) pass; GitProcess does not set GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS.
failure_scenario: authority.git whose packed-refs contains refs/replace/<commit> with no refs/replace directory passes every check (hooks, config, alternates, base ref, pinned file hashes) while git history and ancestry readers see the replaced graph; only the three pinned file blobs are content-hashed, so commit/tree replacement is not caught before constructors run.
evidence: Reproduced with plain git: replace ref created then pack-refs and the empty refs/replace dir removed; (repo/'refs/replace').exists() is False, `git log main` shows 1 commit versus 3 with GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1, rev-parse --verify main unchanged. Did not run inspect_source end to end. grep of substrate/git/process.py found no replace-object env guard. Pre-existing.

summary: runs_result drops outputs beyond the first 20 keys with no partial marker, and a legitimately truncated-looking {'truncated': true} value is indistinguishable from the sentinel.
failure_scenario: A run with 25 output ports returns a preview listing 20 sorted keys; RunResultPreviewV2 has failures_partial but no outputs flag, so the preview reads as the complete output set (I4: partial over dropped). A real output equal to {'truncated': True} collides with the over-2000-char sentinel.
evidence: Read _bounded_mapping (sorted(value)[:20]) and RunResultPreviewV2 fields in core/control.py:1197; no outputs_partial field exists. Not executed. Pre-existing.

summary: registry_rdeps for an unknown component returns an empty successful page, unlike registry_versions which refuses unknown names.
failure_scenario: A mistyped or unregistered component name yields NamePage(items=()), read as 'nothing depends on it' before a change or deletion; ComponentRegistry.rdeps does no existence check.
evidence: Read registry_rdeps (no `component in snapshot.versions` check) and runtime/registry.py:1006 rdeps (builds reverse edges from snapshot, returns sorted(seen) which is [] for any absent name). Not executed. Pre-existing.

summary: system_describe with explicit component_names silently omits requested components that are registered but have no stable version; truncated stays False.
failure_scenario: component_names=['x'] where x is registered but unpromoted returns zero component descriptions with no fault, no marker and truncated=False, so an agent cannot tell 'not described' from 'does not exist or was not asked'. build_component_description does raise for the same case.
evidence: Read build_system_description: `unknown` checks only snapshot.versions, then `if stable_hash is None: continue`. Not executed. Pre-existing.

summary: _reconcile_stale_leases closes a stale active capability lease as released/discarded without any physical reconcile when its binding or LeasedCapability provider is not found.
failure_scenario: A stale active row whose provider is absent from Walker._capabilities or is not a LeasedCapability (activate() validates only the catalog) is transitioned to closed with disposition released/discarded though nothing cleaned the resource, producing a false-complete lease record and hiding the leaked workspace/process from later recovery.
evidence: Read lines 1462-1492: `if binding is not None: ... if isinstance(capability, LeasedCapability): reconcile` is skipped silently and transition_capability_lease runs unconditionally. Not executed; reachability depends on assembly passing catalog and capabilities that disagree. Pre-existing.

summary: runs_result composes status, outputs, failures, accounting and result reference from separate reads taken at different instants.
failure_scenario: A FAILED run resumed and finished between the snapshot read and optional_reference() yields status=failed with a result detail ref pointing at the later success, or failures from a later event window than the accounting cut.
evidence: Read-only trace of runs_result (capability_accounting_snapshot, materialize_run, journal.events, optional_reference are independent reads). Not executed.

summary: result/<seq> and events/<seq> detail URIs accept non-canonical integers (int() accepts ' 5', '+5', '1_0', non-ASCII digits) while accounting and capability-disposals URIs require str(n)==part, so one fact has several addressable URIs.
failure_scenario: constructicon://runs/<id>/events/1_0 resolves event 10; the returned DetailChunk.uri echoes the caller's non-canonical spelling, and cursors/queries key on it. Not an authority bypass.
evidence: Compared the int() parsing at the events and result branches in DetailResolver._resolve with the canonical checks on the accounting and disposal branches. Not executed.

summary: Admission guard tests drive refusals only: grants narrowing covers posture alone (not network, env, tools, timeout), no accepting-path narrowing case, and no cycle test, which is why the dead cycle guard went unnoticed.
failure_scenario: The suite stays green while the cycle detection (finding 1), env/tool/network/timeout narrowing and valid narrowing acceptance are unexercised.
evidence: Read tests/runtime/test_validator.py; grep for 'cycle outside' in tests found nothing; confirmed the cycle guard is unreachable by the probe in finding 1.
